preamble: The shift from [d] to [h] is a rare debuccalization of the voiced alveolar stop to a glottal fricative; voiced stops seldom debuccalize. Its clearest regular case is Chamorro, where Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *d became h in initial and medial position and was lost word-finally (*danum 'water' > hanom, *daRaq 'blood' > håga'), as established by Blust (2000).

examples.note: Blust (2000) gives h as the regular Chamorro reflex of PMP *d (with loss word-finally).

sources: Blust, R. (2000). Chamorro Historical Phonology. Oceanic Linguistics 39(1), 83–122. https://doi.org/10.1353/ol.2000.0002
Greenhill, S. J., Blust, R. & Gray, R. D. (2008). The Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database: Chamorro. https://abvd.clld.org/languages/18
